q1_route.reason: Both routes share the mbr_uuid_to_id opaque premise, so the decision turns on the blocker each adds. Qualifying statx_np needs released-runtime correspondence between the running libc/kernel and pinned Libc source, which public main-branch source cannot establish and we cannot manufacture; statx1 has no local attempt count or byte ceiling on its strictly growing realloc loop, and KAUTH_ACL_MAX_ENTRIES=128 is an SDK declaration, not an allocation proof. The fixed-buffer blockers are all resolvable in-repo.
q1_route.boundDerivableToday: KAUTH_FILESEC_SIZE(128) = 44 + 128*24 = 3116 bytes for the ACL attribute, plus fixed common attributes
q1_route.truncationGuard: probe r5 showed a 32-byte buffer returning rc=0 with full_size=100, so success alone must never admit a capture; full_size > supplied is the refusal
q1_route.caveat: fixed buffers bound the CAPTURE, not the RESOLUTION; mbr_uuid_to_id remains on both routes

q2_absence.preciseReason: VOL_CAP_INT_EXTENDED_SECURITY (attr.h:337-338) is a MOUNT-level statement while XNU's gate is VNODE-level - the attribute is emitted only for a supported, non-null va_acl. Different granularities, so the capability cannot close the gap.

documentedBoundedAlternative.quotedPurpose: to distinguish a kauth_filesec_t with an empty entry (Windows treats this as 'deny all') from one that merely indicates a file group and/or owner guid values
documentedBoundedAlternative.consequence: when the attribute IS returned, entrycount == NOACL is a positive 'no ACL' and entrycount == 0 is a positive 'empty ACL, deny-all'; both documented, in-band and bounded

q2_absence.unresolvedFact: When the attribute is OMITTED there is no bounded, documented, in-band observation that positively separates 'this file has no ACL' from 'this vnode does not supply va_acl'. Not manufactured.
q2_absence.defensibleRule: admit only positive returns; omission is a REFUSAL, never empty; keep the same-descriptor capability as a corroborating premise and an independent refusal trigger, never as a converter from omission to empty

independentObservationOnSelectedCode.finding: the currently selected path already does what the 411 audit forbids
independentObservationOnSelectedCode.behaviour: returns Ok((metadata, vec![])) when filesec_query_property(FILESEC_ACL) reports absent, so an unsupported filesystem presents to policy as 'no ACL writers', i.e. permissively
independentObservationOnSelectedCode.consequence: a fixed-buffer replacement that refuses on omission would be STRICTER than today - the right direction, but a behavioural change to review deliberately; the conflation is live in selected code, not only hypothetical

q3_jointCapture.bracketSemantics: observe_descriptor_with compares before(fstat) == during == after(fstat), where during comes from the SAME syscall as the ACL

realObstacle.why: they live in type-dependent groups (ATTR_FILE_LINKCOUNT / ATTR_FILE_DATALENGTH versus ATTR_DIR_LINKCOUNT) while the bracket accepts both S_IFREG and S_IFDIR; for directories no attrgroup member equals st_size and ATTR_DIR_LINKCOUNT does not generally equal st_nlink
realObstacle.conclusion: a like-for-like during is NOT reconstructible for directories

twoDefensibleRoutes: branch on ATTR_CMN_OBJTYPE and reconcile the directory fields in a reviewed note

keep metadata comparison on fstat and place the bounded ACL read inside the same before/after sandwich - STRICTLY WEAKER, because the ACL is then no longer atomic with during, and must be reviewed as a named weakening
q3_jointCapture.layoutRule: offsets follow the documented getattrlist packing and canonical attribute ordering (pinned bsd/man/man2/getattrlist.2), not request order; never invented

derivableNow: 1 fgetattrlist outer call for the joint capture
1 caller-owned fixed buffer of constant size (fixed common attrs + 3116)
optionally 1 further call and buffer for the volume capability
<= K mbr_uuid_to_id outer calls, where K is the number of mutating-allow ACEs; today's loop resolves only tag == 1 entries whose mask intersects MUTATION, so K <= 128 and is usually far smaller
zero allocations in the 413 decoder, which is borrowed and alloc-free
remainsProfileOrTcbPremise: mbr_uuid_to_id internal allocation, directory-service IPC, cache state, latency and any network effect
q4_derivableVersusPremise.rule: outer call counts are not allocation proofs - the same split already stated for the account observer

q5_nextStep.adapterBoundary: mirror the in-tree pattern that already works: directory_volume.rs::read_uuid_with(file, syscall) takes an injectable fgetattrlist bound to libc::fgetattrlist in production, with a before/after recheck and refusal on incomplete attributes; reusing it makes the parser testable without native fixtures and keeps this off greenfield
q5_nextStep.nextProbe: one descriptor, one call requesting common metadata plus ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED_SECURITY with FSOPT_REPORT_FULLSIZE, reporting the returned bitmap, each attribute offset/length, full_size and entrycount; it MUST include a directory fixture, which r4-r6 do not cover (all used mkstemp files) and which is what question 3 turns on

fixtureMatrix.expect: present, 3116 bytes, fits the fixed buffer

fixtureMatrix.level: runtime; may be unobtainable locally - say so if it is

q5_nextStep.levelDistinction: synthetic-byte decoder tests are code-level and prove no native property; runtime fixtures prove one API response on one machine and OS version, not qualification

concreteDefectIn413Draft.finding: the draft computes explicit_no_acl and never exposes it
concreteDefectIn413Draft.detail: Acl offers only flags() and entry(index), and maps NOACL to count = 0, so a consumer cannot distinguish 'empty ACL, deny-all' from 'no ACL, GUIDs only' - the very distinction kauth.h created the sentinel for
concreteDefectIn413Draft.severity: the same conflation the audit is about, one level deeper
concreteDefectIn413Draft.action: expose the distinction before the decoder informs any policy
concreteDefectIn413Draft.notAnApproval: raised as advice on an unselected private draft, not a review verdict

remainingUnknowns: Released-runtime correspondence between the running macOS 26.6.2 libc/kernel and pinned Libc/XNU source is NOT established and cannot be established from public main-branch source.
No bounded in-band observation positively separates null va_acl from unsupported va_acl when the attribute is omitted.
Whether a local filesystem can produce entrycount == NOACL or entrycount == 0 fixtures at all is untested; if unobtainable, that must be stated rather than simulated.
Directory links/size reconstruction under getattrlist is unresolved and is the pivot for whether joint atomicity can be preserved.
UUID membership service allocation, latency and cache behaviour remain opaque TCB work with no filesystem, home or environment shortcut.
